question: A 25-year-old diver presents with no voluntary motor function and no sensation below the T6 level. Sacral sensation (perianal) and anal sphincter tone are completely absent on examination. Bulbocavernosus reflex returns at 48 hours. What is his ASIA Impairment Scale grade, and what is its prognostic implication?

answers.text: ASIA B — incomplete injury; >50% chance of ambulatory recovery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASIA B is sensory incomplete (some sacral sensation preserved, no motor below injury level). This patient has NO sacral sensation, so ASIA B does not apply.

answers.text: ASIA A — complete injury; motor and sensory function below the injury level including sacral segments S4–S5 is absent; prognosis for recovery below the injury level is poor

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASIA A = complete SCI: no motor or sensory function preserved in the sacral segments S4–S5. The return of the bulbocavernosus reflex signals the end of spinal shock but does NOT change the ASIA grade — it merely confirms the reflex arc is intact. Prognosis for meaningful motor recovery below T6 in a true ASIA A injury is less than 5%.

answers.text: ASIA C — incomplete injury; >3 motor function present, most key muscles grade <3

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASIA C requires preserved voluntary motor function below the injury level (even if most key muscles are grade <3). This patient has NO voluntary motor — ASIA C does not apply.

answers.text: ASIA D — incomplete injury; most key muscles below the injury level have ≥3 strength

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ASIA D indicates functionally useful motor preservation. This patient is completely plegic below T6 — ASIA D does not apply.

overallFeedback.feedback: The ASIA classification hinges on sacral sparing — preservation of any voluntary motor, sensory, or anal sphincter function at S4–S5. Absent all three = ASIA A (complete). Review the ASIA chart (Maheshwari / ASIA 2019 standards).

Correct. ASIA A complete SCI = no sacral sparing (motor or sensory). Bulbocavernosus reflex return merely marks the end of spinal shock — it is a reflex arc phenomenon and does not imply voluntary sacral function or change the ASIA grade.
